newsitem.title: USA: Chesapeake says two La. Chalk wells positive.
newsitem.headline: Chesapeake says two La. Chalk wells positive.

text.p: Chesapeake Energy, whose shares have rocketed over the past year, said two wells in its promising Louisiana Chalk Trend property tested positively in recent weeks.

The Cloud 9 No. 1 well in the Masters Creek Area of the Louisiana Chalk Trend began producing oil and natural gas three weeks ago and has averaged production of 1,950 barrels of oil and 6.8 million cubic feet of natural gas a day since, the company said on Tuesday.
Also, the Lawton 25 No. 1 exploratory well, 11 miles west of Cloud 9, produced at a flow rate of 4,200 barrels of oil and 11 million cubic feet of natural gas a day.

"We feel positive about the results of our second and third (well) completions, which are part of a rapidly expanding production program in Louisiana," Tom Price, vice president of corporate development at Chesapeake, said on Wednesday.
The Lawton well is shut in until October 30 pending completion of a gas pipeline connection.
The Austin Chalk Trend is considered one of the most promising oil and gas prospects in the lower 48 U.S. states.
"When people look at that play and see Chesapeake is the largest leaseholder in the Trend, with over a million acres under license, it can have a significant impact to a company," said Price.
Other operators are currently drilling 11 wells in the area. Chesapeake plans to drill an additional 25 wells next year and 40 to 50 in 1998.
Apart from its Louisiana property, Chesapeake's star has risen on the back of its innovative horizontal drilling technology which has allowed it to exploit properties previously deemed uncommercial.
The company went public in 1993 and the shares rose steadily from the end of last year.
On Wednesday, Chesapeake stock rose $0.50 to $62.125 a share. In the last 12 months to date, the company's stock has gone from a low of $12.375 to a high of $70.25.
